args.name: Safe assessment of alternative wild foods
args.function: Physically examine or test accessible wild food sources, including meadow roots, to establish whether they can safely nourish me and whether preparation is necessary. Report uncertainty rather than assuming edibility.
args.conditions: At tick 96 I have health 100, satiety 41.6, energy 16.05 and no inventory. Berries are known safe but repeated bounded searches found none. Meadow roots were observed previously; their nutrition, toxicity and preparation requirements are unknown to me. No root is currently within observed reach.
args.inputs: An actually accessible food source or a gathered sample; any tools or preparation materials genuinely required by the method. Exact method and prerequisites are unknown.
args.costs: Unknown; specify feasible time, energy, material costs and any risk before testing. Prefer non-ingestive assessment and do not consume unidentified food automatically.
args.effects: Obtain evidence-supported personal food-safety and preparation knowledge through actual examination or trials, if feasible. Do not create food, replenish plants, confer mastery, or claim certainty when the method cannot establish safety.

candidates.function: Inspect an established rooted food plant in reach and its growth needs, and loosen soil or clear competing plants by hand only where the growth model has crust, compaction or competition that limits it.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds, no energy; needs probe. inspect: probe's observation of the plant, 1 round, 0.2 energy. prepare (hand loosening where modeled crust or compaction limits the plant, clearing where modeled competition does) would take 3 rounds at 2 energy each and maintain 1 round at 1 energy; this world's soil and plant model has neither condition, so both take 1 round, 0 energy, and change nothing. cancel: 1 round, 0 energy. Refusals cost nothing: target not in view or reach, or not an established rooted food plant that regrows (fungi, fish, seedlings, non-food and non-regrowing plants).
candidates.effects: target: a plant you see. inspect: probe's record (stock, growth, stage, soil) and the plant's growth contract from the existing rule: growth per ripe unit, growth so far, the least rounds to the next unit at the best rate (growth scale x full daylight), the temperature range (none at minGrowth, full at optimalGrowth), moisture need, waterlogging, harvest pressure 1/(1+depletion/20) and what limits it now. The first inspection records a baseline in your patch record (one square unit around the plant, at most 8 records); later ones report the change. prepare/maintain: 'no corrective work indicated', with the reason; quantity (rounds of work) stays unused. cancel: close the record for target, or all without one. Growth runs only through the existing rule, tended or not; harvest only with gather. No water is carried. Nothing is moved, created, refunded or rewarded.

candidates.function: A two-person conversation session over ordinary tell: propose it to someone you see within 5, each of you joins, then speak with contribute, optionally answering a heard utterance of the other.
candidates.costs: propose, join, resume, contribute: tell's cost, 1 round, 0 energy, 0 material. pause, leave, cancel: no energy, no speech; they only use your action. Study: 1 round; needs tell.
candidates.effects: propose: participants [you, them], topic (max 80), rounds 1-20 until expiry; says an invitation with the session id; only someone who hears it can join. join (with session and topic, the proposer too) and resume say a short tell; contribute says text (max 240) as tell; optional respondsTo: a heard utterance id of theirs in it. Each needs them alive within 5; words count only if they heard them. Active once both joined and heard each other. An answer with new words to their earlier utterance records a reciprocal exchange. Another action (wait is silence), urgent risk or more than 5 apart pauses it; both must resume. leave, cancel, death or expiry ends it. Your record shows only your acts, what you heard and changes within 5 of you. Grants nothing; no reward.

candidates.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
candidates.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

candidates.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
candidates.costs: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
candidates.effects: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

candidates.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
candidates.effects: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

candidates.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
candidates.costs: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
candidates.effects: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

packet.access: Search or retrieve only this experiment abilities with control queries. Missing candidates do not prove a function absent. Full implementation facts remain available in the development handoff; never grant inventory or individual mastery. Require actual physical prerequisites.
